attributes.description: Fires when the PostgreSQL restart counter increases, meaning the database bounced. A point-in-time availability check can miss a restart entirely, so this rule catches the bounce even when pg_up never appeared as 0.
attributes.name: [Supabase OTel] PostgreSQL restarted

investigation_guide.blob:
## PostgreSQL Restarted

The database bounced. Every connection was dropped, all pools were reset, and the cumulative `pg_stat_*` counters restarted from zero.

### Triage Steps
1. Establish whether this was planned (a compute-tier change or maintenance window) or unplanned.
2. For unplanned restarts look for a host-level cause first: an OOM kill, a read-only filesystem, or a full data volume.
3. Check whether the restart was preceded by connection exhaustion or a long-running transaction holding locks.
4. Expect a period of elevated latency afterwards: the buffer cache is cold, so `pg_stat_database_blks_read_total` will rise relative to `blks_hit_total` until the working set is paged back in.

### Tuning
`INCREASE()` is reset-safe, so a database that bounced and reset its own counters is still counted correctly. Raise the threshold above 0 only if you run rolling maintenance that legitimately bounces the database on a schedule.
